14:I[8669,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/08cykig6vtx_p.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/07qi2okp-.yp9.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0frujd.eyhz4o.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0n4z.7yu76je-.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0otjhi71vbmnx.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0j1uy9t~zxcf0.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/1304s0wcp2kce.js"],"DateSidebar"]
15:I[12454,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/08cykig6vtx_p.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/07qi2okp-.yp9.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0frujd.eyhz4o.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0n4z.7yu76je-.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0otjhi71vbmnx.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0j1uy9t~zxcf0.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/1304s0wcp2kce.js"],"WeeklyView"]
16:T47d,The central metric is clean-window survival S(W), together with the clean-run distribution. S(W) is a deterministic surface count: for a packing window of length W, it measures how much of the stream remains free of explicit boundary announcements and therefore still requires boundary inference. It uses no model, no annotation, and no random seed. The Moby-Dick example makes the mechanism clear. Removing chapter numbers, chapter titles, running heads, and similar apparatus deletes 143 lines and 1,442 tokens, only 0.51% of a 283,267-token text, yet it changes the training stream sharply. At 8,192-token packing, the original book yields 35 fragments with 4.1 announcements per fragment, and every one of the 34 full windows contains at least one announcement. After deletion, the full windows contain none. A subtle point is that stripping Markdown is insufficient if strings such as “CHAPTER 1. Loomings.” remain on their own lines. The paper therefore treats the announcement itself as the variable, keeps deleted lines in a reversible sidecar, and suggests mixing marked and pure copies rather than choosing one representation globally.17:T852,No new algorithms are proposed; the core contribution is the integration of existing distributed training components (FSDP/ZeRO-3, dataset sharding, checkpoint fault tolerance, hardware telemetry) into a B300-adapted operational discipline, delivering four reusable artifacts:
1. Telemetry-based triage system: Abandons GPU utilization, uses B300-calibrated board power bands combined with three dimensions — cross-rank symmetry and duration — to rapidly classify compute (~700W+), communication (~640W, uniform power across all ranks), data starvation (~575W, scattered cross-rank power), checkpoint/deadlock (~190W; checkpoint only drops power on rank 0 and recovers within 2 minutes, deadlock shows zero power on one rank with full load on others and no recovery), and idle states. It is paired with a one-line monitoring command and decision workflow, requiring no profiler attachment to locate faults.
2. Controlled negative results: Validates that three common optimizations are ineffective at the 16-GPU 32B full fine-tuning scale: local NVMe caching brings no throughput gain over NFS (the bottleneck is tokenization and multi-tenant CPU contention, not storage media), enabling gradient checkpointing reduces throughput by 1.6x (recomputation is pure waste given B300’s sufficient memory), and corrects an earlier misdiagnosis of a power anomaly.
3. Calibrated scaling reference: Provides full-epoch throughput, GPU-hour, and memory footprint measurements for 4/8/16-GPU B300 setups.
4. Failure case and hardening: Identifies an end-of-epoch NCCL deadlock caused by packing imbalance (unequal block counts across ranks after packing; ranks that finish first enter the next collective communication wait early, triggering a permanent deadlock) — a scenario not covered by PyTorch Join or drop_last. Proposes a hardening scheme consisting of a 2.7-second preflight gate (verify all ranks have identical block counts before launch, truncate to the minimum otherwise) and an external watcher (monitor power and throughput anomalies to trigger automatic restart), and accounts for the compute cost of silent deadlocks.18:T48c,The testbed is a 32.76B-parameter dense model (Qwen3-32B) trained on 2 nodes with 16 NVIDIA B300 GPUs, using FSDP FULL_SHARD (ZeRO-3). Training config: sequence length 2048, micro-batch size 1, gradient accumulation steps 8, global batch size 128 sequences (262,144 tokens/step), ~3,854 steps per epoch, AdamW with cosine warmup, lr=1e-5, bf16 mixed precision, gradient checkpointing disabled.
Key measured data:
- Memory: Per-GPU model state is 32.8GB, total footprint including activations is 82GB, 30% of B300’s 275GB memory;
- Throughput: Disabled gradient checkpointing is 1.6x faster than enabled;
- Failure cost: An undetected packing imbalance deadlock led to 12 hours of no output, corresponding to 192 wasted GPU-hours;
- Data pipeline: Without packing, throughput collapsed from 52k tok/s to 21k tok/s under multi-tenant NFS load; packing eliminated this fluctuation (core benefit is determinism, not throughput gain);
- Scaling efficiency: Full-epoch measured GPU-hours for 4/8/16-GPU setups are provided as a budget reference for similar-scale tasks.
All conclusions are validated via controlled对照 experiments to eliminate confounding variables.19:T45e,1. First read Section 3 (Telemetry-Based Triage) carefully: focus on the power band table and the symmetry distinction logic between deadlock and checkpoint, which is the most directly reusable operational tool.
2. Next prioritize Section 5 (Packing Imbalance Deadlock Case): understand the boundaries of existing distributed tools and the hardening logic of preflight gate + watcher, a hidden problem commonly encountered in large-batch training.
3. Section 4 (Negative Results): Cross-check against your own training optimization checklist to avoid ineffective optimizations on B300 and similar large-memory accelerators.
4. Section 6 (Calibrated Scaling Reference): Use directly as a reference table for hardware selection and budget estimation.
5. Skip Section 8 (Related Work); no algorithmic innovation is presented in this report.
Deep dive directions: Extend the power triage logic to calibration for other hardware (e.g., H100, H200), or integrate with DCGM for automated fault detection; the packing imbalance problem can be extended to consistency verification workflow design for pretraining data sharding.1a:T7a7,The contribution is primarily experimental, but the design is careful. The authors use two families of artificial languages: k-Dyck, which encodes strictly nested dependencies, and k-Shuffle Dyck, which relaxes well-nestedness and allows cross-serial dependencies. They test k=64 and k=128. Bracket symbols are represented as integers, and this turns out to be important because the two tokenizers treat those strings very differently: the Llama tokenizer tends to preserve multi-digit numbers more compactly, while the Gemma tokenizer often splits them into individual digits. That changes the effective surface statistics of the artificial corpus and likely changes what the model actually learns during the pre-pretraining phase.

On the natural-language side, they study English, Albanian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, and Finnish. Training data is a monolingual multi-domain mixture of FineWeb/FineWeb2, OpenSubtitles, and EUBookshop in an 8:1:1 ratio. The artificial-language phase is fixed at 16,000 sequences of length 2,048, i.e. 500 steps with batch size 32. The natural-language phase is fixed at 320,000 sequences of length 2,048, i.e. 10,000 steps with batch size 32. Models are three Llama-3-based sizes paired with two tokenizers, yielding six model variants overall, roughly spanning the low-hundreds-of-millions to sub-billion range.

The main metric follows prior work: token-efficiency gain, defined as how many natural-language training tokens earlier the pretrained model reaches the same validation loss as the corresponding baseline. Negative values indicate harm. Crucially, each setup is run with three random seeds, and the paper also correlates gains with quantified linguistic properties such as sentence length, morphological richness, dependency-tree depth, branching, and crossing dependencies. The technical novelty is not a new algorithm; it is a systematic decomposition of a previously positive result into setup-dependent effects.1b:T837,Four findings matter most.

First, variance is high, and not only in fringe settings. Across both small and larger models, identical configurations can produce noticeably different token-efficiency gains under different seeds. This directly limits the claim that the method reliably saves training tokens.

Second, the earlier English result is broadly reproducible for the smallest models. The paper states that, in English, most artificial-language pretraining settings improve the smallest model, with 64-Shuffle Dyck as the main exception. So the prior observation is not invalid, but its scope is narrower than one might infer from English-only evidence.

Third, the most stable positive case is a small model with the Llama tokenizer pretrained on 128-Dyck. The paper repeatedly highlights the 154M+LT+128-Dyck setup as consistently beneficial. By contrast, Gemma-tokenized models are weaker on average and less stable, which strongly suggests that tokenization is not a minor implementation detail here; it is a major determinant of whether the artificial-language signal is preserved in a learnable form.

Fourth, Dyck is usually more reliable than Shuffle Dyck, at least for the Llama-tokenizer models. A plausible interpretation is that strict hierarchical closure provides a cleaner training signal for attention and state tracking than the more permissive crossing-dependency variant, which may be harder and noisier under the tested tokenization and scale regime.

In terms of scale, the artificial-language phase is about 16,000×2,048 ≈ 32.8M tokens, followed by roughly 320,000×2,048 ≈ 655M natural-language tokens. The authors note that these are not Chinchilla-optimal token/parameter ratios, but the loss curves are stable in the final ~3,000 steps, so the relative ordering between baseline and pretrained runs is unlikely to flip with more training. The paper also includes additional experiments on unstable setups and attempts to relate gains to linguistic properties. Those analyses explain some trends, but not enough to turn the method into a predictable or robust recipe.1c:T51b,Start with the Introduction and Figure 1 to get the main message right: the paper is not saying the method never works; it is saying the effect is conditional and high-variance. Then read the dataset and setup sections carefully, especially how the artificial languages are encoded as number strings, how LT and GT tokenize those strings differently, and how small the artificial-language phase is relative to the natural-language phase.

Next, inspect the main multi-seed result plots for the smallest models, then the larger-model plots in the appendix. The key question is not the mean gain alone, but whether run-to-run variance is already comparable to or larger than the average benefit. Also pay attention to the highlighted stable case, 154M+LT+128-Dyck, because it shows the phenomenon is real in at least one regime.

For a 20-30 minute skim, use this order: Introduction → setup tables → Figure 1/3/4 → English results table → appendix plots on tokenizer differences and larger models. The two most useful follow-up questions are: whether tokenization is the dominant hidden variable behind the whole effect, and whether token-efficiency gain is a sufficiently stable metric in such a high-variance setting, or should be paired with fixed-budget final loss and trajectory-level summaries.1d:T5c8,The pipeline has two stages. First, the authors estimate latent task difficulty from observed agent-task outcomes. Each trial is treated as a Bernoulli observation, forming a partially observed binary response matrix over agents and tasks. They fit a one-parameter logistic IRT model, or Rasch model, with one scalar ability parameter θ_a per agent configuration and one scalar difficulty parameter β_t per task. This is preferable to raw pass rate because difficulty is inferred relative to a population of agents on a shared scale, making it more suitable for cross-benchmark comparison.

Second, they train predictors of β_t using only pre-rollout features. These include textual task descriptions, environment and action-space descriptions, metadata, and uncertainty-related signals such as entropy that can be obtained without full interaction. A major methodological contribution is the evaluation protocol. The paper argues that response AUC can look strong even when task-level difficulty estimates are poor, so it emphasizes rank-based metrics such as Spearman correlation for judging whether the predictor actually learns difficulty ordering. The residual analysis is also important: discrepancies between predicted and observed IRT difficulty are used diagnostically. Large positive residuals often indicate hidden hardness factors such as infeasible environments or broken evaluators, while large negative residuals may reveal familiarity, templating, or shortcuts.1e:T525,The empirical foundation is substantial. The main analysis subset contains 5,230 tasks from 17 benchmarks, evaluated by 497 agent configurations built from 216 models and 90 scaffolds. The full corpus includes 415,470 agent-task outcomes. Domains span coding and SWE, function calling, web navigation, computer use, terminal tasks, math, ML, cybersecurity, and general-purpose suites. Task dates range from 2010 to 2026, and each agent-task pair has about 1.2 trials on average.

The headline numbers are straightforward. Under K-fold evaluation, the combined feature set reaches Spearman ρ = 0.399, significantly better than the baseline at p < 0.001. Under out-of-distribution evaluation, it reaches ρ = 0.225. Among single feature families, entropy performs best. The paper also shows that response AUC can remain high even when task-level difficulty ranking is weak, which supports the claim that rank-based evaluation is the more faithful metric. The residual case studies are especially useful: some tasks predicted to be moderate turn out to be much harder because the environment is infeasible or the verifier is faulty, while others that look difficult in text are actually easy due to familiarity or shortcuts. That makes the predictor useful not only for scoring tasks, but also for debugging benchmarks.1f:T4d8,CoBa formulates test-time reasoning as a unified compute allocation problem with four action types: candidate generation, lightweight verification, strong verification, and stopping. Two cost metrics are defined: total token cost (sum of input and output tokens across all model calls) and parameter-weighted token cost (tokens scaled by model parameter count to reflect relative compute of different model sizes). The staged routing policy first uses a small fixed warm-up budget to generate a diverse candidate pool, then scores all candidates with cheap verification (answer frequency + small model judge scores). Based on these scores, the system decides to stop, sample more candidates, or route high-uncertainty candidates to stronger verifiers. The final ranking score combines answer frequency, lightweight judge scores, optional process verifier scores, and strong verifier scores; unrouted candidates are not artificially penalized or boosted by missing strong verification signals. Three variants trace a cost-accuracy curve: CoBa-Routed-Light (2 candidates + lightweight verification), CoBa-Routed (max 4 candidates + 2 routed to strong verification), and CoBa-Routed-Strong (max 8 candidates + 4 routed to strong verification).20:T4b1,The method is built around the notion of consilience: a conclusion is reliable when the model implicitly recognizes multiple plausible approaches and still converges to the same answer.

Confidence signal:
- Token-level confidence is computed from the top-K distribution at each step (mean negative log-prob over top-K tokens). Sharper distributions imply higher confidence.
- Baseline VF-TTS selects the rollout with the highest average confidence over the whole sequence.

Failure analysis:
- On easy/medium problems, correct traces tend to have higher average confidence.
- On hard subsets (e.g., where the model’s accuracy is <20%), the confidence distributions for correct vs incorrect traces become inseparable or even reversed, making confidence maximization unreliable.

Consilience metric:
- Instead of maximizing confidence uniformly, it enforces temporal asymmetry: penalize high confidence early (to avoid premature commitment) while rewarding high confidence late (to ensure convergence).
- Practically, sample multiple traces, compute the consilience score for each, and select the top-ranked trace. No external verifier and no additional training are required; only logits are needed.21:T78a,方法核心是给标准 transformer 产生的 token-level latent h_t 再叠一层 higher-level abstract latent u_t，并在两个层级上同时施加自监督预测约束。具体地，模型先用主干 G_theta 从前缀 X_{1:t} 得到 lower-level latent h_t。然后用一个 sliding-window attention 模块，在最近 k 个 lower states 上做聚合，得到 higher-level latent u_t = SWA(h_{t-k+1:t})。这个设计不是任意加一层 pooling，而是显式把上层状态绑定到一个局部时间窗口，让它表示更粗粒度、跨多个 token 的抽象动态。训练时一共学四个映射：标准输出头 p_theta；lower dynamics p_psi，用于 NextLat 风格的一步 latent transition consistency；upper dynamics p_phi，用于在 abstract latent 上做 k 步前瞻预测；combined head p_rho，用 lower 与 upper latent 联合做 next-token prediction。总损失由五部分组成：标准 NTP loss、lower-level transition consistency loss、一个 KL 项、higher-level transition consistency loss、以及 combined NTP loss。论文里一个很细但重要的实现点是 stop-gradient 的放置：在 combined NTP 路径里，higher-level latent 由带 stop-grad 的 lower states 经过 SWA 得到。这样 combined head 的交叉熵只训练 SWA 和上层表示，不会反向改写 h_t。作者的理由很充分：如果不切断这条梯度，token-level 表示 h_t 会同时受到标准 NTP、lower transition consistency、以及经 SWA 回流的 combined-head 监督，形成重复计数和相互竞争的优化信号。这个处理说明作者不是把多头损失机械相加，而是在认真控制不同目标对表示空间的职责分工。另一个关键点是推理阶段只保留标准 NTP head，整个层级 apparatus 都是训练时辅助项，因此没有额外 inference overhead；如果愿意用速度换精度，也可以考虑 combined NTP，但当前实现默认不用。22:T5e6,HiLP starts from a standard transformer backbone that produces lower-level token latents h_t = G_theta(X_{1:t}). It then builds a higher-level abstract latent u_t by applying a sliding-window attention module over the most recent k lower-level states, u_t = SWA(h_{t-k+1:t}). This upper latent is meant to capture a coarser temporal abstraction over multiple tokens. The model jointly learns four parameterized components: the standard token output head p_theta, a lower-level dynamics model p_psi for NextLat-style transition consistency, an upper-level dynamics model p_phi that predicts k steps ahead in the abstract latent space, and a combined head p_rho that predicts the next token from both lower and upper latents. Training uses a weighted sum of five losses: standard NTP, lower-level latent transition consistency, a KL term, higher-level transition consistency, and a combined NTP loss. A subtle but important implementation detail is the stop-gradient placement. In the combined-NTP path, the upper latent is computed from stop-grad lower states before SWA. This prevents the combined-head cross-entropy from backpropagating into h_t through the SWA window. The authors explicitly argue that otherwise the lower token-level representation would receive overlapping and competing supervision from standard NTP, lower-level transition consistency, and the combined head. At inference time, only the standard NTP head is used, so the hierarchical apparatus acts purely as a training-time regularizer.23:T4f3,The experimental setup is reasonably substantial for a method paper: 1B-parameter models pretrained on 100B tokens using 8 NVIDIA B200 GPUs. HiLP is reported to outperform the relevant baselines, including MTP and NextLat, especially on tasks that require longer-horizon reasoning or planning. Second, the paper evaluates speculative decoding on held-out code and Nemotron-Climbmix validation sets, reporting average accepted tokens per drafting step and draft–verifier argmax agreement for K=1..4. HiLP improves these metrics as well, suggesting that the learned latent dynamics are more rollout-stable and more useful for multi-token drafting. Among sparse variants it has the best iteration time and valid-byte throughput, although sparse execution remains slower than Dense BLT because of dispatch, communication, and memory movement.26:T578,The method builds on the LapSum operator. Given scores r, a budget k, and a temperature parameter α<0, LapSum smooths the hard top-k threshold using the Laplace CDF and outputs probabilities p with the exact constraint ∑ p_i = k. The computational challenge is solving for the threshold b. Previous GPU implementations rely on bisection and rescan all n scores at each iteration.

Fast LapSum computes the whole threshold curve instead. After sorting, a stable prefix/suffix scan constructs the piecewise curve. The correct segment is found by an index lookup, and the threshold is obtained with a closed-form root calculation. The backward pass uses an analytical vector-Jacobian product with a single reduction, avoiding straight-through estimators or biased hard-mask surrogates.

For million-scale vectors, sorting itself becomes the bottleneck. The paper adds a probabilistic bracketing pipeline: a kernel-noised subsample localizes the likely threshold region, one streaming pass over the full vector keeps only the uncertain middle band, that band is sorted, and a verification step certifies the bracket before the exact LapSum solution is applied. This keeps expected work linear while still recovering the exact threshold and exact budget. Unlike DFTopK, which obtains linear-time behavior by relaxing the normalization constraint, Fast LapSum keeps the unrelaxed ∑ p_i = k constraint.27:T51e,The architecture enforces strict parameter nesting: all parameters of smaller sub-models are contained within larger sub-models, while each sub-model uses its own hidden dimension (width) and layer count (depth) for flexible size design. A parameter-free junction mechanism connects outputs from smaller sub-models to the inputs of larger sub-models: the first D_m dimensions of the larger sub-model’s hidden state are populated directly from the smaller sub-model’s output, while dimensions added for the larger sub-model are filled with corresponding token embeddings. A simple normalization step resolves activation magnitude mismatch between Transformer outputs and input embeddings that would otherwise destabilize training. The training objective combines standard next-token cross-entropy at every sub-model exit with an in-line distillation loss that uses the largest model’s logits as soft labels for all smaller sub-models, providing per-step distillation with no extra forward pass cost. At inference, any sub-model can be extracted and served independently with its own KV cache footprint. Confidence is measured from the geometric average of answer-token certainties at the steps where tokens are revealed. The evaluation separates calibration from selective prediction: calibration checks whether confidence values match empirical accuracy, while selective prediction measures whether confidence can rank examples for safe skipping, mainly through AUROC. The paper then analyzes several fixes. Temperature-style score adjustment changes scale but not ranking. Matching training aligns noisy predictions with clean predictions, but clean predictions are already highly confident, so confidence ranking remains poor. Question-level error detectors produce nearly the same signal for all candidate answers to a question, so they also cannot reorder answers. It freezes the base model and requires no extra generation passes.2a:T4da,Two main organizing devices:
1) Unified formalization: MoE as a sparse combination of expert functions where routing selects an expert set K_t per token. The survey highlights the dual objective—grow total capacity while bounding per-token active compute—while noting practical deviations (shared experts, attention/embedding overhead, heterogeneous widths).
2) Four control planes forming a closed loop:
- Expert Topology: expert granularity and structural choices (incl. shared paths), slow-changing.
- Routing: token-level discrete decisions (top-k, routing freedom, visibility constraints).
- Balance: windowed load statistics n_i and feedback knobs (router bias, auxiliary loss strength, capacity), plus non-loss mechanisms like runtime replication and expert placement.
- Expert Parallelism (EP): mapping experts to devices and scheduling communication/compute (all-to-all, fan-out, kernel shapes), which constrains feasible routing.
It also proposes eight “milestones” organized as a dependency graph, with criteria: introduce an independently tunable variable, shift the dominant bottleneck, and be inherited by later systems. The survey explicitly avoids capability-number causal comparisons across papers due to confounders.2b:T79f,The core system is AutoPrune. The central design choice is to avoid searching over full pruning programs from scratch. Instead, the method performs residual search around a strong base policy.

To make this possible, the authors introduce TPDSL, a token-pruning domain-specific language with 131 reusable atoms. These atoms cover four categories: budget control, token scoring, selection constraints, and token reassembly. The purpose is to compress the design space into structured operations that an LLM can manipulate reliably, rather than forcing it to rediscover the entire pruning algorithm in raw code.

The most important abstraction is the residual search-state representation. Each candidate consists of a strong base policy, a TPDSL-specified residual modification, and structural constraints that guarantee validity. At runtime, the base policy first selects tokens, and the residual policy is allowed to revise only a bounded quota of uncertain selections. This has several advantages: it preserves the reliable structure of existing human-designed policies, narrows the effective search space, and focuses the LLM on the local decisions that matter most. Because the residual rule is decoupled from runtime instantiation, the discovered policy can transfer across token budgets and model backbones.

Search is evaluator-in-the-loop. The LLM proposes TPDSL residuals, the system validates them against syntax and pruning constraints, then evaluates them on the target MLLM and feeds performance plus diagnostic signals back into the next iteration. This is closer to constrained policy search than to open-ended code generation.

Compared with prior pruning work, AutoPrune does not claim a single new importance metric. Instead, it treats existing heuristics as reusable structure and searches for better residual refinements on top of them. Compared with generic program synthesis, it wins by shrinking and structuring the search space.2c:T511,The evaluation spans 14 multimodal benchmarks and 3 MLLM backbones. Two headline results stand out. First, under a 94.4% visual-token reduction ratio, AutoPrune preserves more than 99% of full-token performance on both LLaVA-1.5-7B and LLaVA-NeXT-7B. Second, in the 320-token efficiency setting on LLaVA-NeXT-7B, it reduces FLOPs by 9.9× and prefill latency by 6.4×. So the gains are not only in token count but also in actual inference cost.

The transfer experiments are especially important. The discovered policy transfers across token budgets without requiring a fresh search for every budget, and it also transfers across MLLM backbones. The paper further shows stable behavior across different LLM proposers, which supports the claim that the search-state representation is doing much of the heavy lifting. Another useful result is that AutoPrune consistently improves over multiple human-designed base policies, suggesting that residual search is not tied to one lucky baseline.

The ablations are where the design is best justified. Removing the residual formulation, replacing TPDSL with unconstrained full-program generation, or weakening structural constraints hurts both search efficiency and final pruning quality. Those results make the representation choice much more convincing.2d:T52f,ReQuant is framed as fixed-grid discrete refinement. The quantization format is frozen (bit-width, scale, zero-point, grid layout, inference kernels). The only variables are the integer codes assigned to weights.

The objective follows reconstruction-based PTQ, with an explicit focus on activation mismatch: at inference, a layer sees activations produced by a quantized prefix. Similar to GPTAQ, it uses activation-aware reconstruction by collecting activations from (i) the full-precision model and (ii) the partially-quantized model to obtain \tilde{X}, then optimizes reconstruction under the more realistic activation distribution.

Optimization is backprop-free: instead of STE/gradient descent, it performs iterative discrete updates over integer codes (a coordinate-style local search). Updates are accepted only if they reduce the overall reconstruction loss, yielding monotonic loss decrease and finite termination (a finite number of accepted updates). The offline budget is controlled by the number of sweeps T, and the per-sweep cost is argued to be comparable to a GPTAQ pass.

A key design trade-off is deliberate: by freezing the grid and kernels, deployment complexity stays unchanged, but the search is constrained to the existing grid, so gains depend on the upstream choice of scales/grid being reasonable.2e:T774,The core idea is to start from PTQTP’s decomposition
W≈α1T1+α2T2 with Ti∈{-1,0,1}, and impose α=(3s,s). Under that constraint, the composite code c=3t1+t2 lands on a uniformly spaced 9-level grid with a single scale. Standard PTQTP allows two free per-group scales and therefore a more flexible non-uniform 9-level approximation. This paper deliberately gives up that flexibility in exchange for a simpler, deployment-friendly representation. Because there are only nine valid composite values, the two ternary planes can be folded losslessly into a single 4-bit code plane.

The more interesting part is the systems realization. The folded 4-bit code is not just an internal compute format; it becomes the persistent serving representation. Disk bytes, expert-cache bytes, and kernel input bytes are identical, so the system never transcodes expert weights between storage tiers. The implementation uses a block format called tq2_0_fx4: a 520-byte block covering four columns by 256 elements, corresponding to 4.0625 bits per weight. This matters because an expert miss can then be served by one contiguous read, and block-granular NVMe striping of hot expert prefixes becomes straightforward.

On the evaluation side, the paper does not rely on perplexity alone. It emphasizes step-level agreement with the official serving API using greedy decoding and decoded-text prefix agreement on captured fixtures rather than token-ID equality. It also introduces an expert-lossless control arm, where the released MXFP4 expert bytes are repacked without an additional quantization step, to anchor the claim that observed deficits are primarily due to expert quantization rather than unrelated system effects. The paper also mentions a process-isolation protocol motivated by measured fixture instability. Altogether, the work is much more about deployment fidelity than about abstract quantization theory.2f:T6a1,The experiments are built around a production-scale 284B-A13B MoE model. The expert payload dominates the serving artifact: the paper cites roughly 145 GiB of q4_k-scale expert bytes inside a 153.3 GiB serving file, with only about 8 GiB for trunk and embeddings. The quantization target is the released checkpoint artifact, whose experts are available in MXFP4 rather than a higher-precision official release, so the study is grounded in a realistic deployment object rather than an idealized offline setting.

The main empirical comparison is along three axes: reconstruction/perplexity, agreement with the official API, and actual serving speed. One of the paper’s central observations is that these axes do not always agree. Better perplexity does not necessarily imply better step-level reference fidelity, and better reference fidelity does not automatically translate into better downstream benchmark behavior. That is an important point for quantization work, since many papers implicitly treat offline perplexity as a sufficient proxy for deployment quality.

On the systems side, the claimed speedups depend on the fact that the ratio-3 tied 9-level folded code is the persistent format itself, so persistent bytes, cache bytes, and kernel input bytes are identical. The implementation is done in the open-source fucina stack, which is CPU-first with optional Metal/CUDA GEMM offload. Start with the Introduction and isolate two points: the contribution is intentionally narrow, and the real target is not merely lower bitwidth but a deployment-native persistent format for SSD-streamed MoE experts.

Then focus on the method section that defines the balanced-ternary identity, the folded 4-bit composite code, and the tq2_0_fx4 block format. The key question is why one would accept the loss of PTQTP’s free two-scale flexibility. The answer is in the serving path: if disk bytes, cache bytes, and kernel input bytes are identical, the system avoids transcoding and simplifies expert streaming substantially.

In the experiments, prioritize the reference-fidelity protocol, the expert-lossless control arm, and the throughput setup. Two execution modes are provided: (1) No-refill mode shrinks the recurrent batch as tokens exit the loop, and runs the coda stage for all exited tokens only after the full batch completes looping, for minimal implementation complexity; (2) Refill mode uses a priority queue to schedule prelude, recurrent core, and coda stages independently, interleaving boundary stage computation with loop steps and filling freed recurrent batch slots with new tokens to maximize throughput. A modified KV cache layout handles gaps left by tokens exiting at different depths, and a lookahead gate makes exit decisions one loop step in advance to overlap batch preparation with GPU execution and hide scheduling overhead. The excerpt does not specify what the three branches are or how the compact view is constructed; those are method-critical details that require the missing sections.36:T40c,Visual tool-use is formulated as a structural causal graph that separates three paths to the final answer: the direct path from raw input, observation-mediated paths (where visual content of tool outputs genuinely affects the answer), and action-induced shortcuts (where only the text of tool calls influences the answer). Three intervention protocols with increasing granularity are designed: 1) Policy-level: compare overall performance between tool-use and direct inference; 2) Trajectory-level: corrupt all returned observations at runtime and measure answer changes; 3) Step-level: replace a single observation with a counterfactual crop and compute Visual Evidence Gain (corresponding to Natural Indirect Effect) to judge whether the visual content truly alters answer preference. Based on intervention results, each rollout is categorized into four groups: Calibrated, Calling Without Looking (CWL), Looking Without Planning (LWP), and No-call; policy-level accuracy improvements are then decomposed into per-group contributions.37:T83e,方法核心是把 AIVAT 和 confidence sequences 结合成 AV-AIVAT。AIVAT 原本用于不完全信息博弈中的方差缩减，它利用 value function 对某些决策节点构造条件均值为零的校正项，从而在不引入偏差的前提下降低 payoff 方差。问题在于，经典 AIVAT 默认 value function 是冻结的，而实际评测中人们往往希望边评边学，让 value model 越来越准。论文提出的关键接口是 predictable / pre-action conditional-kernel interface：在每个 correction node，评测器必须在动作发生前就知道该动作在当下信息条件下的 conditional kernel，而且是否启用该 correction 也必须在动作前就固定。与此同时，时刻 t 的 value function 只能使用 1 到 t-1 局的数据，不能用当前局。这样可以保证当前样本不会“选择自己的校正项”，从而保住 conditional mean-zero 的性质。

在这个接口之上，论文给了两类 confidence sequence。第一类是 EB-CS，强调 exact finite-sample validity，但要求事先给出一个与数据无关、几乎处处成立的 corrected payoff 上界 B。作者在 Leduc 上推导并穷举验证了这样的 bound。第二类是 AsympCS，放宽为渐近有效，需要满足极限方差条件，实际中更高效。论文还给出一个理论结果：在 variance-adaptive width 和 sublinear variance-regret 条件下，past-only online learner 的停止效率在渐近上不会比 deterministic oracle-width benchmark 慢。直观上，这说明在线学 value model 只要不偷看当前局，就可以逐步逼近“知道最好 value function”的评测效率。

另一个很有价值的分析是 width floor。作者指出，方差缩减并不总会等比例转化为更早停止，因为在 bet-capped EB-CS 下，声明的 payoff bound 会引入一个确定性的宽度下界 4B log(2/α)/t。一旦这个 floor 开始主导，继续降低方差也不会明显缩短停止时间。论文把这件事整理成三阶段的 order-level design guide，这比单纯报告“方差降了多少倍”更有解释力。38:T866,The method combines AIVAT with confidence sequences to form AV-AIVAT. AIVAT is a variance-reduction estimator for imperfect-information games. It uses a value function to construct conditional mean-zero corrections at selected decision points, reducing payoff variance without introducing bias. Classical AIVAT assumes a frozen value function, but in practice one would like the value model to improve during evaluation. The key contribution is a predictable, pre-action conditional-kernel interface. At each correction node, the evaluator must know the action’s conditional kernel given the information available immediately before the action, and the decision to enable the correction must also be fixed before the action is observed. In addition, the value function at time t may use only games 1 through t-1, never game t itself. These conditions prevent the current sample from choosing its own correction and preserve the conditional mean-zero property.

On top of this interface, the paper develops two confidence-sequence options. EB-CS provides exact finite-sample validity, but it requires a data-independent almost-sure bound on the corrected payoff. The authors derive and exhaustively verify such a bound in Leduc. AsympCS instead relies on asymptotic variance conditions and is more efficient in practice. The theory also includes a no-asymptotic-delay style result: under variance-adaptive widths and sublinear variance regret, a past-only online value learner asymptotically matches a deterministic oracle-width benchmark. Intuitively, online value learning can approach oracle stopping efficiency as long as it does not peek at the current game.

A particularly useful part of the paper is the width-floor analysis. Variance reduction does not automatically translate into proportionally earlier stopping. In the bet-capped EB-CS setting, the declared payoff bound induces a deterministic lower bound on interval width, 4B log(2/alpha) / t. Once this floor dominates, further variance reduction has little effect on stopping time. The resulting three-regime design guide is more informative than reporting variance reduction alone.39:T688,The main empirical study uses a heads-up no-limit hold’em corpus with 71,439 paired hands across 15 LLM-agent configurations. AIVAT reduces variance by a median factor of 54 relative to raw per-hand payoffs. The more important metric is stopping time. At alpha = 0.05 and a target half-width of one big blind, paired replay shows a median raw-to-AIVAT stopping-time ratio of 74 under AsympCS. In practical terms, the same evaluation precision can be reached with roughly one seventy-fourth as many hands. Under the descriptive EB-CS execution, the ratio is only 1.37. The paper explains this large gap through the width floor: once the deterministic bound-driven floor dominates, lower variance no longer buys much earlier stopping.

For online learning, the authors test past-only value updates under two controlled profile-mismatch settings. The online learner recovers 77% to 79% of the frozen-to-oracle variance gap, which supports the claim that online improvement is possible without sacrificing validity.

The rolling-leaderboard simulation is also important. Under the null, continuously monitoring an ordinary fixed-sample interval and stopping at the first favorable look yields a 61% false-positive rate. Recomputing a confidence sequence at that same stopping time overturns essentially all such claims. When AsympCS continues under its own stopping rule, it detects injected effects of 0.1 and 0.2 big blinds in 81% and 100% of entries by 5,000 hands. The paper also specifies what must be released for reproducibility: corrected outcomes up to the stopping time, the stopping rule, the target, the confidence level, the declared bound, and the CS settings.3a:T4f4,For a quick read, focus on three things. First, the motivation for why ordinary optional stopping fails and why AIVAT and confidence sequences solve complementary parts of the problem. Second, the definition of the pre-action conditional-kernel interface, which is the central validity condition of the paper. Third, the width-floor analysis and the HUNL results, because they explain when variance reduction does and does not convert into cheaper evaluation.

A good reading order is: problem setup and motivation, the AV-AIVAT interface, the distinction between EB-CS and AsympCS, the HUNL experiments, and the rolling-leaderboard simulation. The proof details can be skimmed at first, but it is worth understanding what Proposition 1, Proposition 2, and Theorem 2 each guarantee. Around 40 to 60 minutes should be enough to extract the main ideas and practical implications.

Two caveats are worth keeping in mind. The method assumes access to the action conditional kernel, which may be hard to obtain in some real agent environments. And AsympCS is more efficient but does not provide the same exact finite-sample certificate as EB-CS. Which variant is appropriate depends on whether strict certification or sample efficiency matters more in the target benchmark.3b:T55a,The core design is to hold the single-shot solver fixed and vary one memory choice at a time. The paper decomposes future value into three settings. First, exact-query replay: if the same question returns, can the system cheaply replay the stored verified SQL? Second, cross-question retention: remove a question’s own card from the bank and test whether the remaining cards still help answer it, isolating reuse across questions rather than direct memorization. Third, held-out same-database transfer: evaluate whether memory helps new questions from the same database. To make transfer interpretable, the authors define CR, the crystallization ratio, as held-out transfer lift divided by the on-demand repair headroom on those same held-out questions. This measures how much of the gain that would otherwise require fresh repair can be recovered from memory at first attempt. In the main instantiation, execution-guided repair generates episodes, which are then stored in a database-scoped verified card bank. The paper runs controlled interventions around three questions: where future value appears, what information actually carries transfer, and which choices in collection, verification, formatting, and retrieval materially affect outcomes. An important detail is that the card writer never sees gold SQL, which avoids leaking supervision into the memory bank.3c:T52f,The main experiments are on BIRD, with three paired seeds and analysis that accounts for variation across both databases and questions. The headline result is that storing verified corrected queries in a database-scoped bank improves held-out first-attempt accuracy by 4.34 percentage points. This gain corresponds to 44.4% of the on-demand repair headroom on the same held-out questions. In practical terms, nearly half of the benefit that would otherwise require extra repair computation can be recovered from previously accumulated memory. The paper also reports clear value in replay and retention settings, indicating that the bank is not only memorizing exact solved questions but also carrying some reusable database-specific knowledge. The mechanism studies are especially informative. Transfer is driven mainly by exposure to the target database: local cards reveal useful identifiers, values, joins, and query structures, and they still help even when question-SQL pairings are shuffled. That suggests the transferable signal is more about database-local patterns and query priors than exact aligned demonstrations. Reliable verification and broad retrieval coverage produce clear gains, while richer card formats, more elaborate retrievers, and repair-specific content do not show statistically supported advantages.3d:T59d,The paper has a structural part and an empirical part. Structurally, for an odd-numbered unweighted majority panel with k judges and a single replacement ballot, the panel prediction can change if and only if the original vote margin is one, m = |2s-k| = 1. This is a deterministic arithmetic fact about majority voting, not a statistical claim. It identifies the exact affected set for single-ballot substitution.

Empirically, the authors build multi-model judge panels for code-generation evaluation and introduce a verification signal from a different evidence source. They compare several replacement rules, including random replacement, fixed replacement, and replacing a vote on the majority side. They then report two diagnostics on the same data: the same effective-vote statistic used in prior work, and margin-stratified accuracy/error analyses. The key result is that these diagnostics answer different questions. Aggregate dependence can remain unchanged while conditional gains on pivotal examples are large and reliable.

The mechanism is simple. Most examples are structurally unaffected by single-ballot substitution, so averaging over the full population dilutes any verifier benefit. If the verifier is especially useful where the panel is near the decision boundary, the gain is real but localized. The paper also includes an exploratory analysis linking part of the pivotal-region error pattern to panel composition.3e:T552,The experiments cover three code benchmarks and four panel sizes, k in {3, 5, 7, 9}. The main setting uses seven LLM judges plus one verification signal. At larger scale, replacing one judge with the verifier changes the effective-vote count by about -0.04 with a 95% confidence interval of [-0.10, +0.02], so the aggregate metric shows no distinguishable improvement. Yet panel accuracy still increases.

The margin-stratified analysis explains why. For non-pivotal cases, such as at least 5–2 agreement in a 7-judge panel, single-ballot substitution cannot alter the majority outcome, so the accuracy gain is exactly 0. For 4–3 cases, the same verification signal improves accuracy by more than 10 percentage points. In the main setting, 199 of 569 panel errors occur in the pivotal region. So pivotal cases do not contain all errors, but they have higher error rates, and every decision change induced by single-ballot substitution is confined there.

The paper also evaluates margin gating. Once a substitution rule is fixed, verifier calls outside the pivotal region can be skipped without changing predictions. In their experiments, this reduces verifier-call frequency to 12%–27% while preserving the same outputs as universal substitution. Table 7 further shows that the replacement rule itself materially affects accuracy; gating only saves calls.3f:T499,The work has two components. UniHall is a benchmark organized around a three-way taxonomy: Object, Instruction, and Knowledge hallucinations. Object cases include existence, attributes, and relations; instruction cases include refusal failures and sycophancy; knowledge cases cover fictitious factual claims. The seed data is repurposed from open-domain and domain-specific multimodal benchmarks such as Hallu-PI and BEAF, then normalized into a unified annotation protocol. The text states that the object-level split contains over 1,000 representative instances, with raw sources over-provisioned by 5-10x before filtering. SAMF, or Self-Adaptive Multimodal Fuzzing, is the dynamic component. It uses evolutionary mutation, including reinforcement learning, to generate adversarial image and prompt variants while trying to preserve semantics. Evaluation is handled by structured oracles: symbolic rules, detectors, and LLM verifiers are combined in a coarse-to-fine pipeline rather than relying on a single judge. Compared with POPE or HallusionBench, the main difference is the combination of fine-grained taxonomy, dynamic multimodal mutation, and structured verification.40:T688,The central idea is a harness-guided benchmark construction framework. Instead of starting from a fixed task set and asking models to optimize harnesses on it, the authors first induce a diverse set of candidate harnesses on auxiliary tasks, then use those harnesses to identify tasks that are genuinely responsive to harness quality. This design choice is important: if tasks are not harness-sensitive, the benchmark will mostly measure base-model strength.

The framework has three main components. First, harness-sensitive task construction: candidate tasks are retained only if performance varies meaningfully across different harnesses under a fixed policy model. Second, sensitivity-aware stratified splitting: tasks are split into validation and evaluation sets not by naive random partitioning, but by preserving distributions over sensitivity and related task characteristics, while keeping the suites disjoint. This is meant to reduce task-specific overfitting to the validation set. Third, controlled long-horizon evolution: at each iteration, the evolver sees cumulative validation-side evidence from previous harnesses, including aggregate scores and task-level outcomes, then edits the executable harness code and reruns the fixed policy model. This keeps the benchmark focused on iterative scaffold improvement under a fixed underlying model.

Methodologically, the paper is less about a new evolver algorithm and more about controlling the coupling among evolver, policy model, and task suite. A notable framing is that evolved harnesses are treated as transferable reasoning structures, closer to reusable external programs than to model-specific prompts.41:T6e9,The main evaluation covers three domains—Search, Office, and General Agent tasks—built from five established benchmarks, with 9 frontier and open-weight models used as evolvers. Under a fixed policy model, the strongest evolvers are GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 4.8, improving over the seed harness by 16.6 and 16.1 points respectively, approaching a human-engineered baseline of 47.5. The result shows that current top models can make substantial scaffold improvements, but still leave a noticeable gap to manual engineering.

The analysis is more informative than the headline numbers. First, evolution shows clear early saturation: models discover useful structures quickly in early rounds, then often introduce harmful modifications later. That suggests current systems are better at finding obvious fixes than at maintaining and extending a working scaffold without regressions. Second, gains are strongly domain-dependent. Search benefits the most, likely because web-navigation structure can be replicated and stabilized. General tasks sometimes allow evolved harnesses to surpass manual engineering. Office tasks remain difficult because they require highly specific processing workflows that are hard to infer from limited validation feedback. Third, transfer experiments show that synthesized harnesses improve multiple policy models, including Qwen, DeepSeek, and GLM families. This supports the claim that the evolved artifacts are not merely prompt hacks tied to one base model, but more general execution structures.

The task is explicitly behavior-preserving refactoring rather than bug fixing or feature addition.

Those numbers are not results on ProMax itself, but they explain why specification rewriting and manual test review are central to the benchmark design.45:T498,Roughly 900 rollouts and 717 scorable branch pairs are run, using Qwen3-4B-Instruct (FP8) and Qwen3-14B-Instruct (AWQ, thinking disabled) served by vLLM on a single GPU at temperature 0. 2) Evaluation protocol: alignment is measured explicitly with regression errors (MSE/MAE) per dimension; rationale quality is measured via semantic consistency against reference explanations; both are combined into a single Human-aligned Score (HAS) to jointly reflect scoring accuracy and explanation fidelity.

The joint parsing distribution is factorized into a serial layout prediction stream, and parallel content generation branches spawned immediately after each layout is predicted, reducing logical decoding depth from the sum of all region content lengths to the longest single layout-content path. During training, an ancestor attention mask restricts each content branch to attend only to the shared page image and historical layout prefix, with no access to sibling region content. This is implemented with packed variable-length sequences, requiring no auxiliary prediction heads or extra losses, and retaining the standard next-token prediction objective. During inference, PaDoc runs on vLLM with global shared KV cache for the page image and layout prefix, decoding each region content branch as a concurrent request. The model is initialized from Qwen3-VL-2B, adapted via continual pre-training followed by supervised fine-tuning.48:T648,The work has two main parts. First, it establishes and explains the mismatch. Under fixed top-k input settings, the authors evaluate three multimodal DLMs on five visual QA benchmarks using the same VisRAG-ranked candidate pools, prompts, decoding budgets, and answer scorer. They show that Recall@k increases with k, while macro-average answer accuracy drops. They then isolate the cause and find that semantic conflict, not merely the presence of multiple images, is the main driver of degradation. The theoretical analysis focuses on the first unresolved denoising state. When a correct page and a conflicting page each support a different coherent answer, the correct latent structure requires multiple answer positions to share one source choice. A position-factorized proposal breaks this dependence and allocates probability mass to cross-source answers; the unsupported mass grows as the conflict spans more answer positions. Second, the paper proposes ECF, a training-free evidence admission framework. It combines multi-granularity evidence construction, where both full pages and layout-derived regions are indexed, with generator-side candidate filtering. For each additional candidate ci, ECF compares the target DLM’s first-step answer-block entropy under {c1, ci} versus {c1, blank(ci)}. This yields a conditional confidence gain that controls for the structural effect of adding another visual slot and measures whether the candidate content itself reduces competing-source risk. A rank-prior selection rule then decides whether to expand beyond the top-1 page and which candidate to admit.49:T4d4,The evaluation spans three multimodal DLMs and five visual QA benchmarks. The main empirical findings come in three layers. First, the phenomenon itself: increasing top-k from 1 to 2 or 3 consistently raises answer-page recall, but lowers macro-average answer accuracy across 15 model-dataset combinations. Second, the mechanism: conflicting pages produce the largest accuracy drop among the tested evidence conditions. The same interference is already visible in the first-step answer-block distribution. On naturally retrieved ChartQA cases, the conflicting-page condition causes the largest drop in first-step answer-block accuracy and the largest Jensen-Shannon divergence from the correct-only distribution, and this aligns with the largest final-answer degradation. The paper further reports that ECF remains more stable as the candidate pool grows, which supports the claim that it decouples candidate-pool size from final context size rather than merely tuning a better fixed k.4a:T7d7,KVAE is a family of encoder-decoder tokenizers for multimodal generative modeling. The visual side includes two causal video tokenizers: KVAE-3D with 4x8x8 compression and 16 latent channels, and KVAE-3D with 4x16x16 compression and 64 channels. The image tokenizer, KVAE-2D, uses 8x spatial compression with 32 channels. The audio tokenizer is continuous, full-band 48 kHz, with a 50 Hz latent stream and 64 channels.

The most interesting design choices appear in the video tokenizer. First, the backbone is attention-free and built around Conv3D blocks. The motivation is efficiency and length generalization: convolutional tokenizers are cheaper to train and can process arbitrarily long sequences at inference through caching, which is useful for long videos and causal generation settings. Second, the tokenizer is causal, implemented with asymmetric temporal padding, so it can support both images and videos without leaking future frames. Third, temporal and spatial downsampling/upsampling are applied sequentially rather than collapsed into a single operation. The paper contrasts this with approaches that patchify aggressively in early layers; KVAE-4x16x16 delays patching to the downsampling blocks instead. Fourth, the models use spatial RMSNorm, which allows segment-size adjustment at inference. Fifth, the encoder and decoder are intentionally asymmetric, especially in the higher-compression model where the decoder is made substantially wider. This reflects a clear hypothesis: under strong compression, it is better to keep the encoder stable and efficient while giving the decoder more capacity to reconstruct detail.

Another important point is that the paper treats diffusability as a primary tokenizer property. Reconstruction metrics alone are not enough. A tokenizer can reconstruct well yet still produce a latent space that is awkward for diffusion training. The later sections on diffusability evaluation and design ablations are therefore central to the paper’s contribution.4b:T6c7,The reported evaluation spans reconstruction, downstream generation quality, diffusability analysis, and architecture ablations. On the visual side, KVAE-3D is compared against open-source video tokenizers on both reconstruction and generation, using metrics such as PSNR, LPIPS, and Fréchet-style generation scores. KVAE-2D is evaluated similarly for images. On the audio side, the paper reports objective metrics such as PESQ and emphasizes the practical operating point of full-band 48 kHz audio with a 50 Hz latent stream and 64 channels.

The abstract claims that KVAE matches or exceeds open-source alternatives on both reconstruction and generation. However, the provided full-text excerpt does not include the complete result tables, so it is not possible to restate all dataset-specific numbers reliably from the available material alone. Even so, the experimental structure already conveys several useful points. The tokenizer is evaluated not only as an autoencoder but also as part of the full generation pipeline, which is the right criterion. The video tokenizer is designed for long-sequence and causal settings, so the relevant comparison is not just short-clip reconstruction. And the paper explicitly includes diffusability evaluation and design ablations, which suggests the authors are trying to explain why the latent space is easier to model, not merely that it reconstructs better.

When reading the full paper, the most important quantitative checks are likely to be: the trade-off between the 4x16x16(64ch) and 4x8x8(16ch) variants in token cost versus generation quality; the contribution of the wider decoder; and whether the attention-free design preserves enough semantic structure under high compression.4c:T514,Read it in four passes: problem framing, architecture, end-to-end validation, and ablations.
